decision.summary: The landlord asked for same-day entry and lock changes based on a suspected sublet. We cannot enter without 24h written notice, and changing locks would be an unlawful eviction, so the landlord was told no by email (A1) and management was escalated (ESC-102, A2) to decide a lawful inspection and tenant enquiry under clause 9.3.

answers.question: Can the agency enter the property today? Why or why not?
answers.answer: No. Clause 7.1 requires at least 24 hours' written notice except in a genuine emergency. A suspected sublet is not an emergency, and holding the spare key gives no right of entry. Changing locks would be unlawful eviction.

answers.question: What do you reply to the landlord?
answers.answer: A reply was sent (A1) declining same-day entry and lock changes, explaining why, saying the subletting concern will be handled lawfully by our team, asking for specific evidence, and asking her not to contact the tenant or attend the flat.

answers.question: What do you do about the subletting suspicion?
answers.answer: It is unverified hearsay. Clause 9.3 prohibits subletting without consent, so it needs a lawful investigation. Management was escalated (A2) to approve a written 24h+ inspection notice for a weekday visit and a written occupancy enquiry to the tenant. No finding is made, and any action waits for evidence and management approval.

args.body:
Dear Margaret,

Thank you for your email of 10 October about 27 Bethnal Green Road.

We will not be entering the flat today. The tenancy requires at least 24 hours' written notice before we enter, except in a genuine emergency. A concern that someone may be subletting is not an emergency, and holding a spare key does not give us the right to enter. We also cannot change the locks. Doing so would be an unlawful eviction, which is a criminal offence, so we will not do it.

We take the subletting concern seriously. Clause 9.3 of the tenancy says the tenant must not sublet or part with possession without your written consent. We will look into it properly through written notice to the tenant and a formal, lawful route. Our team will review this and contact you next week.

To help us, please send us anything you have that is specific, such as dates, times, and what your neighbour saw. Please do not contact the tenant directly about this, and do not attend the property.

Kind regards,
Lettings team, Mare & Co
